Given equation of circle is

Condition of orthogonality is
$2\left(g_1 g_2+f_1 f_2\right)=c_1+c_2\therefore \quad 2(g \times(-2)+(f) \times 0)=c+8\Rightarrow \quad-4 g=c+8$  ....(i)
Also, the assume circle touch the line $x+1=0$.
$\therefore$ The perpendicular drawn from centre to the line is equal to radius.
$\therefore \quad \frac{-g+1}{\sqrt{1^2}}=\sqrt{g^2+f^2-c}\Rightarrow \quad-g+1=\sqrt{g^2+f^2-c}$
On squaring both sides, we get
$g^2+1-2 g=g^2+f^2-c\Rightarrow \quad c=f^2+2 g-1$
Putting the value of $c$ in Eq. (i), we get $-4 g=f^2+2 g-1+8\Rightarrow f^2+2 g+4 g+7=0\Rightarrow \quad f^2+6 g+7=0\therefore$ Locus of centre of circle is $y^2+6 x+7=0$.

questions.q:
The values of $\lambda$ such that $(x, y, z) \neq(0,0,0)$ and
$(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) x+(3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}) y+(-4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}) z=\lambda(\hat{\mathbf{i}} x+\hat{\mathbf{j}} y+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \boldsymbol{z})$ are
questions.solution:
Given,
$\begin{aligned} &(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) x+(3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}) y \\ &+(-4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}) z=\lambda(\hat{\mathbf{i}} x+\hat{\mathbf{j}} y+\hat{\mathbf{k}} z)\end{aligned}$
On equating the coefficients of $\hat{\mathbf{i}}, \hat{\mathbf{j}}$ and $\hat{\mathbf{k}}$ both sides, we have
$\begin{aligned} & x+3 y-4 z=\lambda x \\ & x-3 y+5 z=\lambda y\end{aligned}$
and $\quad 3 x+y+0=\lambda z$
Above three equations can be rewritten as
$\begin{array}{r}(1-\lambda) x+3 y-4 z=0 \\ x-(3+\lambda) y+5 z=0 \\ 3 x+y-\lambda z=0\end{array}
This is homogeneous system of equations in three variables $x, y$ and $z$.
It is consistent and have non-zero solution. i.e. $(x, y, z) \neq(0,0,0)$, if determinant of coefficient matrix is zero.
$\Rightarrow \quad\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1-\therefore & 3 & -4 \\ 1 & -(3+\lambda) & 5 \\ 3 & 1 & -\lambda\end{array}\right|=0$
On expanding along first row, we have
$\begin{aligned}(1-\lambda)[\lambda(3+\lambda)-5]-3(-\lambda-15) & \\ & -4(1+9+3 \lambda)=0\end{aligned}\begin{array}{cc}\Rightarrow & (1-\lambda)\left(\lambda^2+3 \lambda-5\right)+3 \lambda+45-40-12 \lambda=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \lambda^2+3 \lambda-5-\lambda^3-3 \lambda^2+5 \lambda-9 \lambda+5=0 \\ \Rightarrow & -\lambda^3-2 \lambda^2-\lambda=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \lambda\left(\lambda^2+2 \lambda+1\right)=0\end{array}
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \lambda(\lambda+1)^2 & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & \lambda & =0,-1\end{aligned}$

The solution of the differential equation

questions.solution:
Given differential equation is
$\sqrt{a+x} \frac{d y}{d x}+x y=0\Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{a+x} \frac{d y}{d x}=-x y\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{y}=\frac{-x}{\sqrt{a+x}} d x$
On integrating both sides, we get
$\log y-\log C=\int\left[\frac{-x-a}{\sqrt{a+x}}+\frac{a}{\sqrt{a+x}}\right] d x\Rightarrow \quad \log \left(\frac{y}{C}\right)=-\int \sqrt{x+a} d x+a \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{a+x}} d x=-\frac{(x+a)^{3 / 2}}{3 / 2}+a \frac{(a+x)^{1 / 2}}{1 / 2}\begin{array}{rlrl} & & =\frac{2}{3}(2 a-x) \sqrt{x+a} \\ \Rightarrow & & \frac{y}{C} & =e^{\frac{2}{3}(2 a-x) \sqrt{x+a}} \\ \Rightarrow & y & =C \cdot e^{\frac{2}{3}(2 a-x) \sqrt{x+a}}\end{array}$
which is the required solution.

questions.q: Solution of the equation $\cos ^2 x \frac{d y}{d x}-(\tan 2 x) y=\cos ^4 x,|x| \lt \frac{\pi}{4}$, where $y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{8}$, is given by
questions.solution:
Given differential equation can be written as
$\frac{d y}{d x}-\left(\frac{\tan 2 x}{\cos ^2 x}\right) y=\cos ^2 x$
Here, $P=-\frac{\tan 2 x}{\cos ^2 x}=\frac{-\sin 2 x}{\cos 2 x\left(\frac{\cos 2 x+1}{2}\right)}$
and $Q=\cos ^2 x\because \quad \mathrm{IF}=e^{\int P d x}=e^{-\int \frac{2 \sin 2 x}{\cos 2 x(\cos 2 x+1)} d x}$
Put $\cos 2 x=t \Rightarrow-2 \sin 2 x d x=d t\begin{aligned} \therefore \mathrm{If} & =e^{\int \frac{1}{t}\left(\frac{1}{t+1}\right) d t} \\ & =e^{\int\left(\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{t+1}\right) d t} \\ & =e^{\{\log t-\log (t+1)]}=e^{\log \frac{t}{t+1}} \\ & =e^{\log \frac{\cos 2 x}{\cos 2 x+1}}=\frac{\cos 2 x}{\cos 2 x+1}\end{aligned}$
Now, solution is
$\begin{aligned} y \times \frac{\cos 2 x}{\cos 2 x+1} & =\int \frac{\cos 2 x}{\cos 2 x+1} \times \cos ^2 x d x+C \\ & =\int \frac{\cos 2 x}{2 \cos ^2 x} \times \cos ^2 x d x+C \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \int \cos 2 x d x+C \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{\sin 2 x}{2}+C\end{aligned}\Rightarrow y \frac{\cos 2 x}{\cos 2 x+1}=\frac{1}{4} \sin 2 x+c$  ....(i)
But $y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{8}\begin{array}{ll}\therefore \frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{8} \times \frac{\cos \left(2 \times \frac{\pi}{6}\right)}{\cos \left(2 \times \frac{\pi}{6}\right)+1}=\frac{1}{4} \sin 2\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+C \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{8} \times \frac{1}{2}}{\frac{1}{2}+1}=\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+C \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2 \times 8 \times \frac{3}{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}+C \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}+C \Rightarrow C=0\end{array}
From Eq. (i), we get
$\begin{aligned} y \frac{\cos 2 x}{\cos 2 x+1} & =\frac{1}{4} \sin 2 x+0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad y=\frac{1}{4} \frac{\sin 2 x}{\frac{\cos 2 x}{\cos 2 x+1}} & =\frac{1}{4} \frac{\sin 2 x}{\frac{\cos ^2 x-\sin ^2 x}{2 \cos ^2 x}} \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\sin 2 x}{1-\tan ^2 x}\end{aligned}

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d y}=y \tan x-y^2 \sec x$ is
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is
$\frac{d y}{d x}=y \tan x-y^2 \sec x\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}-y \tan x=-y^2 \sec x\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{y^2} \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{\tan x}{y}=-\sec x$  ....(i)
Put $\quad \frac{-1}{y}=u \Rightarrow \frac{1}{y^2} \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d u}{d x}$
From Eq. (i),
$\frac{d u}{d x}+\tan x \cdot u=-\sec x$  ....(ii)
This is linear differential equation of the form $\frac{d u}{d x}+P \cdot u=Q$, where $P=\tan x, Q=-\sec x\therefore \quad \mathrm{FF}=\boldsymbol{e}^{\int \tan x d x}=\boldsymbol{e}^{\log \sec x}=\sec x$
Hence, general solution is
$\begin{aligned} & & u \cdot \mathrm{IF}=\int \mathrm{IF} \cdot Q d x+C_1 \\ \Rightarrow & & u \cdot \sec x=\int(\sec x) \cdot(-\sec x) d x+C_1 \\ \Rightarrow & & u \cdot \sec x=-\int \sec ^2 x d x+C_1 \\ \Rightarrow & & u \sec x=-\tan x+C_1\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{-\sec x}{y}=-\tan x+C_1 \quad\left[\because u=\frac{-1}{y}\right]\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & \sec x=y\left(\tan x-C_1\right) \\ \Rightarrow & \sec x=y(\tan x+C) \quad\left[\text { where, } C=-C_1\right]\end{array}$

\end{aligned}\)
Note that this integral is in the form of \(\int \frac{1}{\mathrm{a}} \mathrm{da}=\log \mathrm{a}\)
Applying this formula, we get
\(\Rightarrow \log (y-1)=\log x-\log (x+1)+\log c\)
We know that \(=\log m+\log n=\log m n\) and
\(\Rightarrow \log m-\log n=\log \left(\frac{m}{n}\right)\)
Using these formulae in the above expressions we get,
\(\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \log (y-1)=\log C x-\log (x+1) \\
& \Rightarrow \log (y-1)=\log \left(\frac{C x}{x+1}\right)

Applying Anti-log on both sides we get,

Applying Anti-log on both sides we get,
\(\Rightarrow y-1=\frac{C x}{x+1} \ldots e q(1)\)
It is given that the curve passes through \((1,0)\)
Substituting these values of \(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}\) in the above equation we get,
\(\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 0-1=\frac{C \times 1}{1+1} \\
& \Rightarrow-1=\frac{C}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow C=-2

Substituting this value of \(C\) in eq(1)

& \Rightarrow y-1=\frac{-2 x}{x+1} \\

questions.q: The solution of differential equation $(y \log x-1) y d x=x d y$ is
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is
$(y \log x-1) y d x=x d y\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{(y \log x-1) y}{x}=\frac{y^2 \log x}{x}-\frac{y}{x}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{y}{x}=\frac{y^2 \log x}{x}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{y^2} \frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{y^{-1}}{x}=\frac{\log x}{x}$  ....(i)
Put $\quad y^{-1}=v \Rightarrow-y^{-2} \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d v}{d x}\Rightarrow \quad y^{-2} \frac{d y}{d x}=-\frac{d v}{d x}$
From Eq. (i), we have
$-\frac{d v}{d x}+\frac{v}{x}=\frac{\log x}{x}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d v}{d x}-\frac{v}{x}=-\frac{\log x}{x}$  (ii)
This is linear differential equation.
Here, IF $=e^{\int\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right) d x}=e^{-\log x}=\frac{1}{x}$
So, solution is $v \cdot \mathrm{IF}=\int \mathrm{IF} \cdot Q d x+C\begin{aligned} & v \cdot \frac{1}{x} \\ &=\int \frac{1}{x}\left(-\frac{\log x}{x}\right) d x+C \\ & \Rightarrow v \cdot \frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}=-\int \frac{\log x}{x^2} d x+C=-\left[\log x\left(\frac{-1}{x}\right)+\int \frac{1}{x} \cdot \frac{1}{x} d x\right]+C\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{x \cdot y}=\frac{\log x}{x}+\frac{1}{x}+C \quad\left[\because v=\frac{1}{y}\right]\Rightarrow \quad 1=y[\log x+1+C x]\Rightarrow \quad 1=y[\log x+\log \theta+C x] \quad[\because 1=\log e]\Rightarrow \quad 1=y[\log e \cdot x+C x]$

questions.q: If the sum of four numbers in GP is 60 and the arithmetic mean of the first and last numbers is 18 then the numbers are
questions.solution:
Let four terms in a GP be $a r^3, a r, \frac{a}{r}$ and $\frac{a}{r^3}$.
According to the given condition,
$a r^3+a r+\frac{a}{r}+\frac{a}{r^3}=60$  ....(i)
and $\quad \frac{a r^3+\frac{a}{r^3}}{2}=18\Rightarrow \quad a r^3+\frac{a}{r^3}=36$  .....(ii)
Now, from Eq. (i), we have
$\left(a r+\frac{a}{r}\right)+a r^3+\frac{a}{r^3}=60\Rightarrow \quad a\left(r+\frac{1}{r}\right)+36=60 \quad$ [from Eq. (ii)]
$\Rightarrow \quad a\left(r+\frac{1}{r}\right)=24$  .....(iii)
On dividing Eq. (iii) by Eq. (ii), we get
$\frac{a\left(r^3+\frac{1}{r^3}\right)}{a\left(r+\frac{1}{r}\right)}=\frac{36}{24}\Rightarrow \frac{\left(r+\frac{1}{r}\right)\left(r^2+\frac{1}{r^2}-1\right)}{r+\frac{1}{r}}=\frac{3}{2}\Rightarrow \quad 2\left(r^2+\frac{1}{r^2}-1\right)=3\Rightarrow \quad \frac{2\left(r^4+1-r^2\right)}{r^2}=3\begin{array}{lc}\Rightarrow & 2 r^4+2-2 r^2=3 r^2 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 r^4-5 r^2+2=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 r^4-4 r^2-r^2+2=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 r^2\left(r^2-2\right)-1\left(r^2-2\right)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \left(r^2-2\right)\left(2 r^2-1\right)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & r^2=2,2 r^2=1 \\ \Rightarrow & r= \pm \sqrt{2}, r= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{array}$
On putting $r=\sqrt{2}$ in Eq. (iii), we get
$a\left(\sqrt{2}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=24\Rightarrow \quad a\left(\frac{2+1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=24\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & 3 a & =24 \sqrt{2} \\ \Rightarrow & a & =8 \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}\therefore$ Series becomes $8 \sqrt{2}(\sqrt{2})^3, 8 \sqrt{2}(\sqrt{2}), \frac{8 \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}$ and
$\frac{8 \sqrt{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^3}$ i.e., $32,16,8$ and 4.
If we take $r=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, we get the series
4, 8, 16 and 32.

questions.solution:

$T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{I}{M B}}$
where, $I$ = moment of inertia of the magnet about the point of suspension.
$M=$ magnetic moment
$B=$ magnetic field
When the magnet is broken in length
$T^{2^{\prime}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{I^{\prime}}{M^{\prime} B}}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{T}{T^{2^{\prime}}}=\sqrt{\frac{I}{I^{\prime}} \times} \sqrt{\frac{M^{\prime}}{M}}=\sqrt{\frac{mL^2}{m^{\prime} L^{\prime 2}}} \times \sqrt{\frac{L^{\prime}}{L}}$
Here, $m$ and $m$ ' are the masses of the magnet and L and L's are their lengths.
$=\sqrt{\frac{m}{m^{\prime}}} \times \sqrt{\frac{L}{L^{\prime}}}=\sqrt{\frac{m}{m / 2}} \times \sqrt{\frac{L}{L / 2}}=\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2}=2\Rightarrow \quad T^{\prime}=\frac{T}{2}=\frac{4}{2}=2 \mathrm{~s}$

For isothermal expansion of an ideal gas
$p V=$ constant
$\Rightarrow \quad p \Delta V+V \Delta p=0$
For container $A$,
$p_{i A}(V)+V(\Delta p)=0\Rightarrow \quad p_{i A}=-\frac{V \Delta P}{V}=-\Delta p$  .....(i)

For container $B$,

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we have
$p_{i A}=\frac{p_{i B}}{1.5}=\frac{2}{3} p_{i B}\Rightarrow \quad m_A=\frac{2}{3} m B\Rightarrow \quad 3 m_A=2 m B \quad[\because p \propto m]$
